name: Hishuley Carmel preserved olives
description: Concentrations of whole and fragmented olive stones in structures are interpreted as evidence of preserved table olives.

impact.note: One site's hedged evidence for preserved table olives, a modest addition to diet with nothing later shown to rest on this site.

date.label: Approximately 6700–6400 years BP
date.basis: The paper reports individual combined ages of 6656–6450 BP and also summarizes the structures as about 6700–6500 years ago; rounded BCE endpoints cover both summaries using the conventional 1950 BP reference.

events.statement: Concentrations of whole and fragmented olive stones in structures are interpreted as evidence of preserved table olives.

evidence.supports: The paper compares relatively less-fragmented pits in Hishuley Carmel structures with highly fragmented pits at Kfar Samir and interprets them as evidence for preserved table olives; cultivation is unsettled.

events.caveats: Pickling or dry salting is an archaeological interpretation; the researchers cannot establish which method or whether the trees were cultivated.

earliest_record.rationale: Date of the supported scoped case; no global priority is implied.

caveats: Pickling or dry salting is an archaeological interpretation; the researchers cannot establish which method or whether the trees were cultivated. The sampled pits were 48% counted as intact (including halves) and 52% fragmented, not a majority intact; the interpretation rests on their context and comparison with a more heavily crushed oil-extraction assemblage.

research.note: Independent review checked the cited passages for the facets marked reviewed; archaeological interpretation and source-specific limitations remain as stated.
